context.chief_complaint_en: Holes in maize leaves and something boring inside the stem

questions.ask_en: Is the damage in the whorl (top funnel) or in the stem lower down?
questions.why: Whorl feeding with frass indicates fall armyworm; stem tunnelling with dead heart indicates stem borer.

questions.ask_en: Do you see sawdust-like waste inside the whorl?
questions.why: Fresh frass strongly indicates fall armyworm.

primary.label: Fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) or maize stem borer (Busseola fusca)

differentials.label: Maize stem borer (Busseola fusca)
differentials.ruled_out_because: Cannot rule out - stem tunnelling is consistent with stem borer.

differentials.label: Striga hermonthica
differentials.ruled_out_because: Striga causes stunting and scorching, not boring holes or stem tunnelling.

diagnosis.confidence_basis: Holes in leaves plus stem boring point to a chewing insect pest, not a fungal rot.
diagnosis.confidence_ceiling_reason: Need larval identity and damage location to reach confirmed.

immediate.action_en: Open the whorl of 10 plants in 5 spots and look for caterpillars and fresh frass.

preventive.action_en: Scout fields weekly from emergence through vegetative stage.

do_not.text_en: Do not apply any pesticide until larvae are confirmed and a registered product is named by your extension officer.
do_not.reason: Unverified dosage is the highest-risk failure mode.

escalation.trigger_en: If more than 20% of plants show whorl damage or larvae are found on most scouted plants.
escalation.referral: Contact your ward agricultural extension officer with one affected plant.

follow_up.success_indicator_en: No new frass and no fresh ragged holes.

review.human_notes: Gold: FAW vs stem borer for maize leaf holes + stem boring

context.chief_complaint_en: Cassava leaves have yellow mosaic patterns and plants are stunted

questions.ask_en: Are the leaves twisted or misshapen in addition to the yellow pattern?
questions.why: Twisting confirms cassava mosaic disease over nutritional deficiency.

differentials.label: Cassava brown streak disease
differentials.ruled_out_because: Brown streak causes root necrosis and brown stem lesions, not mosaic leaf patterns.

differentials.label: Nitrogen deficiency
differentials.ruled_out_because: Nitrogen deficiency yellows older leaves uniformly, not in mosaic patches.

diagnosis.confidence_basis: Classic mosaic symptoms; whitefly presence would confirm.
diagnosis.confidence_ceiling_reason: No field confirmation of whitefly vector.

immediate.action_en: Rogue out severely infected plants and destroy them away from the field.

preventive.action_en: Use certified virus-free cuttings at next planting.

do_not.text_en: Do not save cuttings from infected plants for replanting.
do_not.reason: CMD spreads through infected planting material.

escalation.trigger_en: If more than 30% of plants show mosaic symptoms.
escalation.referral: Contact your extension officer or NRCRI for resistant variety recommendations.

follow_up.success_indicator_en: No new plants showing mosaic symptoms.

context.chief_complaint_en: Tomato plants suddenly wilt during the day and recover at night

questions.ask_en: If you cut the stem near the base, is the inside brown?
questions.why: Brown vascular tissue indicates bacterial wilt.

differentials.label: Fusarium wilt
differentials.ruled_out_because: Fusarium causes one-sided yellowing before wilting; bacterial wilt causes sudden collapse.

differentials.label: Drought stress
differentials.ruled_out_because: Drought-stressed plants do not recover at night.

diagnosis.confidence_basis: Day-night wilting pattern is classic for bacterial wilt.

immediate.action_en: Remove and destroy wilted plants including roots; do not compost.

preventive.action_en: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for at least 3 years.

do_not.text_en: Do not plant tomato, pepper, or potato in this field for at least 3 seasons.
do_not.reason: Ralstonia survives in soil and plant debris for years.

escalation.trigger_en: If more than 10% of plants show wilting.
escalation.referral: Contact your extension officer; bring a wilted plant with roots.

context.chief_complaint_en: Maize plants are stunted with purple leaves and no visible insect damage

questions.ask_en: Do you see small purple-flowered weeds emerging near the maize base?
questions.why: Striga emergence confirms the parasite; absence does not rule it out because most damage is underground.

differentials.label: Phosphorus deficiency
differentials.ruled_out_because: Phosphorus deficiency also causes purple leaves but does not appear in patches tied to weed pressure.

differentials.label: Fall armyworm
differentials.ruled_out_because: No visible insect feeding or frass reported.

diagnosis.confidence_basis: Stunting and purple coloration without insect signs is characteristic of Striga parasitism.
diagnosis.confidence_ceiling_reason: Need to confirm striga presence by digging roots.

immediate.action_en: Dig up one stunted plant and check the roots for small attached striga shoots.

preventive.action_en: Rotate with non-host crops such as legumes for at least 2 seasons.

do_not.text_en: Do not apply nitrogen fertilizer hoping to cure stunting without confirming the cause.
do_not.reason: If the cause is striga, nitrogen will not solve the parasite problem.

escalation.trigger_en: If more than 30% of plants are stunted across the field.
escalation.referral: Contact your extension officer for striga-resistant variety recommendations.

follow_up.success_indicator_en: No new stunting in subsequent rows.

review.human_notes: Gold: striga damage mimics nutrient deficiency

context.chief_complaint_en: Small round holes in stored cowpea seeds

questions.ask_en: Do you see small brown beetles moving in the container?
questions.why: Live beetles confirm active infestation rather than old damage.

differentials.label: Post-harvest weevil damage
differentials.ruled_out_because: Weevils typically damage whole grains, not stored cowpea with round exit holes.

diagnosis.confidence_basis: Round exit holes in cowpea are the diagnostic signature of Callosobruchus.

immediate.action_en: Inspect the whole container; separate heavily damaged seeds and destroy them.

preventive.action_en: Use hermetic bags or airtight containers for future storage.

do_not.text_en: Do not mix new seed with old seed from the same container.
do_not.reason: Live beetles will re-infest the fresh seed.

safety_caveats: No chemical treatment recommended without extension officer

escalation.trigger_en: If more than 10% of stored seed is damaged.
escalation.referral: Contact your extension officer for approved storage treatment.

context.chief_complaint_en: Groundnut plants have yellow mottled leaves and are stunted with small seeds

questions.ask_en: Do you see clusters of small black insects on young leaves?
questions.why: Aphid presence confirms rosette transmission vector.

differentials.label: Nutrient deficiency
differentials.ruled_out_because: Mottle patterns and stunting together are more consistent with virus than simple deficiency.

differentials.label: Groundnut leaf spot
differentials.ruled_out_because: Leaf spot causes dark brown lesions, not yellow mottling.

diagnosis.confidence_basis: Mottle, stunting, and small seed are the classic rosette triad.

immediate.action_en: Remove and destroy severely mottled plants to reduce virus spread.

preventive.action_en: Plant rosette-resistant varieties at next planting.

do_not.text_en: Do not save seed from diseased plants.
do_not.reason: Seed-borne spread is possible and resistant varieties are the main defense.

escalation.trigger_en: If more than 15% of plants show mottling.
escalation.referral: Contact your extension officer for resistant variety recommendations.

context.chief_complaint_en: Rice leaves are mottled yellow and plants are dying in patches

questions.ask_en: Do you see small metallic beetles on the leaves?
questions.why: Beetle presence confirms RYMV transmission vector.

differentials.label: Bacterial leaf blight
differentials.ruled_out_because: Blight causes wilting and pale streaks, not yellow mottle.

differentials.label: Nitrogen deficiency
differentials.ruled_out_because: Deficiency yellows older leaves uniformly, not patch dieback.

diagnosis.confidence_basis: Yellow mottle and patch dieback are characteristic of RYMV.

immediate.action_en: Remove and destroy infected plants to slow spread.

preventive.action_en: Plant RYMV-resistant varieties and manage water levels carefully.

do_not.text_en: Do not move equipment between infected and healthy paddies without cleaning.

safety_caveats: No chemical cure for viral infection

escalation.trigger_en: If more than 10% of paddies show mottle.
escalation.referral: Contact your extension officer for variety recommendations.
